chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from an-Nadr from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara from Umar ibn Hanzala from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The voluntary prayer on Friday, if you wish, is from the beginning of the day, and whatever you intend to pray on Friday; if you wish, you may hasten it, so you pray it from the beginning of the day, whichever part of the day you wish, before the sun declines.
ai.seo_question: When can voluntary Friday prayers be performed according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of performing voluntary Friday prayers (salat al-tatawwu') at any point during the day before the sun declines, offering believers flexibility to either hasten or delay these acts of devotion. It reflects the Shia juristic view that the specific prohibition of voluntary prayers on Friday applies primarily to the time immediately preceding the obligatory congregational prayer, rather than the entire day. This ruling underscores the spiritual importance of Friday as a day of increased worship and preparation for the communal gathering.
